reason: Re-opened packet.js veda 18 --verse 1.131.3: Sāyaṇa glosses mithunāḥ as patnīsahitā yajamānāḥ and later dvau jāyāpatirūpau janau (husband and wife); he raises the objection that women lack the right to sacrifice, answers yadyapi striyāḥ nāsti pṛthagadhikāras tathāpi … asty eva striyā adhikāraḥ sa ca patyā saha, and concludes tasmāt mithunā yajñaṃ tatasre ity etat yuktam, so the reading is his own conclusion (citing Mīmāṃsā 6.1), not merely reported. ‘Share the rite with her husband, though not perform it alone’ is exactly his limit, stated as his (rule 6). Wilson’s long note on mithunāḥ agrees. Plain sense: 1.131.1 has Dyaus and Earth bowing to Indra and verse 2 onward turns to the men who worship; fair. verse.js ok (ref Rig Veda 1.131.3, at [130,3]); entry-check ok, 41 words; ‘couples’ is one quoted word. Revision 207804 is hymn 1.131, dated 2019-07-26 by the API. Attacks tried on all nine lines; none lands.
